newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire fighting centres on Goma-Mugunga showdown.
newsitem.headline: Zaire fighting centres on Goma-Mugunga showdown.

text.p: Militias on opposing sides of central Africa's worst ethnic faultline fought for control of territory near the eastern Zairean city of Goma as night fell on Friday.

A Reuters correspondent in the city, seized by Zairean rebels about a week ago, saw a mortar round explode on the outskirts, coming from the direction of Mugunga, a vast refugee camp controlled by armed Rwandan Hutu exiles.
Locals in Goma said they were scared the Hutus, who had fought alongside Zairean soldiers, might try to launch a counter-attack to recapture the hungry city.

Sporadic mortar, anti-aircraft and small-arms fire boomed and crackled on the edges of town and local rebels said fighting on the road to Mugunga had raged for the last three days, despite a one-sided ceasefire the rebels declared on Monday.
The fighting in east Zaire seems to be centring on a showdown between Goma and Mugunga, which have in effect become twin cities separated by about 15 km (eight miles).

"Today we have managed to push the enemy back," rebel leader Laurent Kabila told reporters in his Bukavu headquarters 100 km (60 miles) to the south. He said battles near the camp had raged for the past few days.

He proposed a buffer zone along the frontline to get food to refugees in Mugunga. He said the security zone could be policed by some 500 soldiers sent by the international community -- but not France.
"We will withdraw our troops half a kilometre (550 yards) and we are asking that the enemy withdraw their troops half a kilometre the other way to create a security zone," Kabila said.
Goma, nerve centre until last week of the world's biggest humanitarian aid operation for 1.2 million Rwandan and Burundian refugees, is in the hands of local rebels, many of them Tutsis.
Soldiers from just across the border in Tutsi-led Rwanda have backed them.
On the other side of the lines are the Rwandan Hutus who fled their homeland two years ago after carrying out the genocide of 800,000 Tutsis, as well as other victims.
Rwanda says it wants the refugees of Mugunga -- half of them under 16 -- to come home, and the fighters among them to be disarmed and brought to justice for genocide.

When the fighting began three weeks ago, the Hutus were fighting alongside soldiers from Zaire's ill-disciplined and unpaid army. The rebels say there are still some Zairean soldiers fighting them from inside Mugunga.

It is unclear how many of the 400,000 refugees who made Mugunga the world's biggest refugee city last week were still in the camp, where many people have already died as conditions rapidly sink into squalor.
